experimental_method: CO2 saturated with water in a high-pressure bomb (glass beads and spray catcher); gas from the CO2-rich phase passed continuously through the bomb, expanded, and its water collected in an absorption train and weighed per litre of expanded gas at S.T.P.
quality_remarks: Authors report a sudden jump in water content at about 1000 atm at 75 C that was not quantified (possible critical mixing or soap contamination); that region is not tabulated. Temperature scale and pressure gauge not stated. Table II ratios are derived.
not_extracted_tables: Table II (ratio of mole fractions of water in the CO2-rich and water-rich phases): derived by authors from Table I and earlier solubility data

row_counts.Table I: printed 39 filled cells (19 pressure rows incl. empty 300 atm row, 4 temperature columns); written 39 data rows + 4 label rows

extraction_notes: Text layer matched the 300 dpi image in every cell; matrix restacked by script. Sanity: water content at fixed T has a minimum near 50 to 100 atm then rises; increases with T at fixed P above 25 atm.
needs_pass2_reason: text layer clean, every cell matched image, but the layout restack is a manual transform
pass2_diff: Table I: 39 (P, T, value) tuples identical between pass 1 (long) and pass 2 (matrix); the empty 300 atm row agrees.
